# nuxt-backend-billing: the API

The public names of the catalog, plans, checkout, the portal, feature gates, plan quotas and credits, each with the first sentence of its doc comment.

The file ships inside the package, so it describes exactly the version in `node_modules`. The
core skill, `nuxt-backend`, lists every public name in its own `references/api.md`.

## Auto-imported composables

| Composable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `useBilling()` | Reactive billing state plus the full subscription lifecycle — checkout, gift, portal, plan change and undoing a scheduled one, cancel/uncancel, pause/resume — linked to your auth user. |
| `useFeatures()` | Reactive feature-gating for the current user — the SaaS access primitive. |
| `useCredits()` | Reactive prepaid-credit balance for the current user, plus a `topUp()` checkout and a `refresh()` re-sync. |
| `usePricing()` | The app's plans and credit packs as a pricing page shows them — every plan with its monthly and yearly price, what a year saves, its trial and the credits it grants per cycle; every pack with its price per credit and which is the best value — read through the scaffolded `getPricing`, in the visitor's currency where the catalog prices it. |
| `useOrders()` | The signed-in customer's billing history — past charges straight from the provider's orders API, plus the per-order invoice link. |
| `useUsage()` | Consumption history for a credit meter, read from the provider's events API — the events your server ingested when it spent credits. |

## Components

| Component | What it renders |
|---|---|
| `<PricingTable>` | A complete pricing table, rendered on the server: plan cards from the live pricing (`usePricing`, the scaffolded `getPricing`), a monthly / yearly switch with what a year saves, subscribe / switch / cancel actions, credit packs compared credit for credit, a contact card, and a customer-portal link. |
| `<BillingCheckoutLink>` | A link that opens a checkout for the caller's billing entity. |
| `<BillingPortalLink>` | A link that opens the billing customer portal for the caller's billing entity, through the app's `generateCustomerPortalUrl`, on click. |
| `<BillingHistory>` | The customer's past charges with their invoice links — every row read live from the billing provider (this package stores no order ledger), so what renders is what the provider will show on the invoice. |
| `<UsageHistory>` | Metered consumption, event by event, straight from the provider's events API — the same records that drew the credit balance down. |
| `<UpgradePrompt>` | What someone whose plan lacks a feature sees: a sentence naming the plans on sale that include it, in pricing order, and a link to the first of them on the pricing page (`/pricing?plan=<key>`). |
| `<CancelFlow>` | Cancelling takes one step; a save offer is one optional step (LIFECYCLE). |
| `<WithdrawalButton>` | The EU withdrawal button (LIFECYCLE; Consumer Rights Directive Art. |

## Import paths

### `nuxt-backend/billing`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `defineBillingCatalog()` | Declare the billing catalog (typed identity: its keys stay literal, so `keyof typeof catalog.discounts` names its promotions). |
| `ALL_BILLING_EVENTS` | The provider's full webhook catalog. |
| `setupReferrals()` | Set the referral program up in its own backend file (`backend/referrals.ts`). |
| `setupBilling()` | Configure billing for subscriptions, discounts, prepaid credits, and gift purchases — linked to your auth users and cached reactively inside the `backend` component (so consumers add nothing to their own schema). |

## CLI

### `npx nuxt-backend billing sync`

Push backend/billing.catalog.ts — meters, custom fields, feature/credit benefits, plans (a product per monthly and yearly price, trials, usage prices, tax behaviour; retired plans archived) and packs — to the billing provider, store the webhook endpoint's secret on the deployment, write billing.generated.ts (find-or-create, never deletes; drift reported) and load the deployment's products. Sandbox writes the deployment .env.local names; production writes the production deployment.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--env`: Target environment: sandbox | production (default: the environment the deployment bills in, read from its BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT, else sandbox)
- `--dry-run`: Print the plan without creating anything
- `--webhook`: Provision the webhook endpoint at this URL (default: <site>/billing/events of the deployment written; pass "off" to skip)
- `--force`: Store the webhook endpoint's secret even over a BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET the deployment already holds
- `--adopt`: Adopt existing objects (products, meters, custom fields): key=<id>[,key=<id>…] — recorded as-is, benefits untouched
- `--json`: Print the outcome as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: { environment, dryRun, deployment, log: [{ action, kind, key, id?, note? }], generated, webhook: { url, action: "created" | "exists" | "would-create" | "skipped", secret: "stored" | "kept" | "not-stored" | "none", note? }, products: { status: "synced" | "failed" | "skipped", note? } }.

## Environment

| Name | Capability | Read on | Tier | Without it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BILLING_ACCESS_TOKEN` | billing | deployment | optional | billing queries return empty and checkout actions fail on invocation |
| `BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | billing | deployment | optional | billing events are rejected — entitlements refresh only on demand (syncEntitlements) |
